item.content:encoded:
Korean girl confused after S'porean date takes sofa seat, questions dating etiquette in TikTok video
She assumed he did not like her.
Photos from Canva and TikTok/ dada_dahae
Is it normal for men to give up the sofa seat for their dates?
A recent TikTok video by a Korean woman in Singapore has sparked debate after she said a Singaporean guy didn't offer her the sofa seat on a first date.
The woman, who goes by @dada_dahae, on TikTok, posted a video on Nov. 23 sharing her experience and questioning if this behaviour was common in Singapore.
Speaking to Mothership, the 20-year-old said her intention in sharing the video was never to generalise or criticise Singaporean men.
"I simply wanted to share what I perceived as a cultural difference and learn more about different perspectives and values. I'm genuinely grateful to everyone who shared their thoughts," she said.
Dating in Singapore
Da Hae shared that they had gone on a first date to a Japanese restaurant.
The guy, who is a year younger, had approached her at an MRT station and asked for her contact details.
They eventually started chatting and later arranged a date.
When they arrived, she opened the door, and he went in, heading straight for the sofa seat, leaving her with the normal chair seat.
According to Da Hae, this was a stark contract from the Korean's dating culture, where men always give girls the sofa seat.
If they do otherwise, especially on a first date, that means they have "really bad manners", she explained in her video.
Da Hae told Mothership that she had always believed that asking a date which seat they prefer before sitting down is a "small gesture of consideration and good manners", regardless of gender.
She was confused and wondered if this was his indirect way of showing that he wasn't interested in her.
Da Hae’s date reached out to her that same night, saying he hoped to see her again.
She was surprised at this, she shared in her video.
Da Hae additionally shared with Mothership that she decided not to pursue things further with the guy as she felt that they had different expectations of dating and relationships during the date.
Cultural difference
In her video, Da Hae questioned if she was being "too Korean" and sought opinions from Singaporean girls.
Responses in the comments were divided, with some saying they preferred for their dates to give them the sofa seat.
One netizen even jokingly commented something she always said to her sons, "If you take the sofa seat, the girl will leave you."
Some, on the other hand, said that it did not matter to them as long as they had a good time on the date.
Da Hae shared with Mothership that she has since realised that individual values can differ just as much as cultural norms.
"Many people commented that they had never considered offering the sofa seat a matter of good manners, while others said that a seat was simply a seat. I found it interesting that a gesture I was so familiar with might not be important to someone else at all," she said.
She further added:
"One of the most interesting perspectives was that some people choose the inner sofa seat because it gives them a better view of their surroundings, allowing them to look out for their partner's safety.
Reading that comment made me realise that there might be other ways of showing consideration that I had never thought about before."
